# Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory

## SYNOPSIS

Queues a value in a running passive proxy session, for the server to pull.

## SYNTAX

```
Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory [-Name] <string> [-HostName] <string> [-Key] <string> [-Value] <string> [-Clock <DateTimeOffset>] [-Ns <int>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory cmdlet adds a value for the item -Key of the host -HostName to the store of the passive proxy session named in -Name; the server takes it with the next proxy data it pulls. The host must be one the server's configuration gives the proxy. Objects with HostName (or Host), Key, Value and, optionally, Clock bind by property name, so a batch can be piped in. -WhatIf shows what would be queued.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Queue one value

```powershell
Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory -Name 'dmz-proxy' -HostName 'web-01' -Key 'app.requests' -Value 42
```

The value waits in the session's store until the server pulls it.

### Example 2: Queue a series with past clocks

```powershell
$start = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddMinutes(-3).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
0..2 | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Host = 'web-01'; Key = 'app.requests'; Value = 10 * $_; Clock = $start + 60 * $_ } } |
    Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory -Name 'dmz-proxy'
```

Each object binds by property name; -Clock takes a date, Unix seconds or a clock.
